title: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
name: THE TWO-TRAY TEST
goal: A loud conclusion still has to pass inspection.
steps:
1. Imagine Trays — Imagine two trays.
2. Name Sides — Name the left SUPPORTS IT and the right DOESN’T FIT.
3. Sort Facts — Drop only visible facts into them—no feelings disguised as evidence.
4. Switch Sides — Now cover the fuller tray and read the neglected one silently.
5. Balance Verdict — Finish with a verdict that can hold both sides without pretending they weigh the same.

title: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
name: WORST CASE, WITH EXITS
goal: A worst-case story loses size when it gains a route.

2. Build Exits — Under it build four rungs: WHAT HAPPENS; WHAT I DO NEXT; WHO OR WHAT HELPS; HOW RECOVERY COULD BEGIN.
3. Add Likely — Add a fifth rung for the outcome that is actually most likely.
4. Climb Route — Move through the five steps once in your mind.
5. Act Now — Then take the first coping action available now.

ritualText:
PLAY EMOTION JENGA

PLAY TIME
60–90 seconds

GOAL
Pull one feeling from the stack and see what is actually holding.

1. Name Stack — Name two or three feelings and place each on a separate mental block.
2. Pull One — Temporarily bracket one block with the phrase ‘not deleted—just outside this test.’
3. Check Remainder — Observe what changes in the remainder: body location, urge, story, intensity, or nothing at all. Keep one difference.
4. Rebuild Stack — Restore the removed block. Repeat only if useful, then rebuild the complete stack before finishing.

WIN
✓ The emotional stack revealed which block was actually carrying the weight.

• Do not use urge feeding as proof that an impulse is correct.
• Keep self-control in sight when the urge narrows attention.
• Take one safer choice seriously when the urge feels overwhelming.
• The urge is real; craving escalation is still optional.
• Let self-control have more influence than impulse obedience today.

FORMULA FLOW
Name Stack → Pull One → Check Remainder → Rebuild Stack

PAUSE
Stop if the game causes numbness, feeling unreal or disconnected, suppression, or pressure to erase a valid feeling.
This is a self-help exercise, not emergency or medical care.
